findings.title: A symlink inside the new dev-server fs.allow directories (_data/workbench/ or ts/) that points outside them is followed, so a path such as _private/ is served through /@fs/; the recorded claim that _private/ stays unreachable is not an invariant.
findings.evidence: ts/vite.config.ts fs.allow change and its comment. Reproduced: ln -sfn ../../outside-repo-sim _data/workbench/evil-symlink; GET /@fs/<repo>/_data/workbench/evil-symlink/secret.txt returned 200 with the outside file. Vite isFileLoadingAllowed compares path prefixes without realpath. No CI, schema or governance check refuses symlinks there.
findings.consequence: A committed symlink (a one-line mode 120000 add in a diff) would expose the developer's local _private/ portfolio through the dev server. Not a regression: before this phase the default allow-list was the whole repository root.

notes: Security review standing in for the built-in /security-review (owner ruling, 2026-10-06; idea 000595), triggered by the ts/vite.config.ts dev-server file-access change. Dispatched by the Session Manager in its own scratch clone at 0f043854. The reviewer gave one major finding and no explicit verdict line; recorded as reject because the owner ruled on 2026-10-09 that it be fixed before merge (a check refusing tracked symlinks under _data/workbench/ and ts/, a dev-server guard rejecting /@fs/ paths whose real path leaves the allow-list, and an accurate comment).
